title: Assessment of neurodegeneration and neuronal loss in aged 5XFAD mice
protocol: Wash free-floating brain sections with 1× PBS 5 times, each for 5 minutes, to remove anti-freezing solution completely.
Dilute DAPI stock solution (0.1 mg/mL) in 0.0001% FJC working solution at a ratio of 1:1000.
Stain brain sections with 0.0001% FJC working solution containing DAPI dye for 20 minutes.
Wash brain sections with ddH2O three times to remove extra FJC solution.
Recover brain sections in 1× PBS.
Mount brain sections on slides with Fluorescence Mounting Medium.
Place cover glass on the slides.
Remove bubbles from under the cover glass and remove extra mounting medium.
Dry the mounted slides in the dark overnight (12–14 h) at room temperature.
Seal coverslips with nail polish.
Store mounted slides at 4°C for up to 1 month before imaging.
Take pictures of degenerated neurons in cortex and hippocampus using an Olympus BX51 microscope with a 20× objective lens.
Use filter cube WU-#1 (dichroic mirror DM400, excitation filter BP330-385, barrier filter BA420) to visualize DAPI.
Use filter cube WB - #2 (dichroic mirror DM500, excitation filter BP450-480, barrier filter BA515) to visualize FJC.
For each mouse brain sample, stain three to five serial sections for quantification.
Picture the entire brain region for quantification.
Open pictures with Fiji-ImageJ software.
Use the “Measure” module to calculate the density of degenerated neurons by measuring the brain area.
Use the “Analyze Particles” module to count the number of degenerated neurons.
Statistically analyze the density of degenerated neurons among several groups using GraphPad Prism 6 software.
Wash brain sections with 1× PBS for 3 times, 10 minutes each time.
Permeabilize sections in 0.3% Triton X-100 in 1× PBS for 30 minutes.
Incubate sections in blocking buffer (5% normal donkey serum and 1% BSA in 1× PBS) for 1 hour at room temperature.
Dilute primary antibodies of anti-cleaved caspase-3 (1:100) and anti-NeuN (1:500) with blocking buffer.
Incubate sections in primary antibodies overnight (12–14 hours) on an orbital shaker at 50 rpm, 4°C.
Wash sections with PBST washing buffer for 3 times, 10 minutes each time.
Prepare secondary antibody solutions of donkey anti-rabbit IgG Alexa Fluor® 594 (1:1000) and donkey anti-guinea pig Alexa Fluor® 488 (1:1000), or fluorophores of your choice, with blocking buffer.
Incubate sections with secondary antibodies for 2 h at room temperature to visualize primary antibodies.
Wash sections with PBST three times, each time for 10 min.
Incubate sections with 100 ng/mL DAPI solution to stain cell nuclei.
Mount brain sections on slides with Fluorescence Mounting Medium.
Put cover glass on the slides and push off bubbles.
Remove extra mounting medium.
Dry the mounted slides in the dark overnight (12–14 h) at room temperature.
Wash brain sections with 1× PBS for 3 times, 10 min for each time.
Mount sections on gelatin-coated slides and allow them to dry for at least 1 h at room temperature.
Perform Nissl staining as shown below.
Mount brain sections on slides with neutral balsam.
Put cover glass on the slides and push off bubbles.
Remove extra neutral balsam.
Take pictures of brain sections using an Olympus BX51 microscope under bright-field with a 20X objective lens.
Stain three to five serial sections for each mouse brain sample.
Picture the entire brain region for quantification.
Open images with Fiji-ImageJ software.
Use the "Measure" module to calculate neuronal density by measuring the brain area.
Use the "Analyze Particles" module to count the number of total neurons.
Statistically analyze neuronal density in given brain areas (cells/mm²) among several groups using GraphPad Prism 6 software.
Measure neuronal density in the dentate gyrus of hippocampus using immunofluorescent staining with anti-NeuN antibody.
Combine immunofluorescent staining with confocal imaging for analysis.
